title: How AI learns from examples
intro: AI learns like a detective collecting lots of clues. People show it many examples, and each one has a label, like a photo marked 'apple'.
From thousands of examples it finds patterns: apples are usually round, red or green, with a little stem.
Good examples teach it well. Wrong or confusing examples teach it mistakes. So the examples matter a lot!

game.prompt: Help a robot learn what an apple looks like. Does each example help it or confuse it?

items.text: A clear photo of a red apple, labelled 'apple'
items.explain: A clear photo with the right label is a great example.

items.text: A photo of a tomato, labelled 'apple'
items.explain: The label is wrong, so the robot learns that tomatoes are apples.

items.text: A photo of a green apple, labelled 'apple'
items.explain: Apples come in different colours. Variety helps the robot recognise all of them.

items.text: A very dark, blurry photo, labelled 'apple'
items.explain: If you can't see the apple, the robot can't learn from the photo either.

items.text: A photo of a banana, labelled 'apple'
items.explain: Another wrong label. The robot might start calling bananas apples.

items.text: A photo of a half-eaten apple, labelled 'apple'
items.explain: Apples don't always look perfect. Real-life examples help the robot.

quiz.question: What is a label in AI training?
options: A name that tells the AI what's in an example
quiz.explain: A label tells the AI what each example shows, like 'apple' or 'cat'.

quiz.question: What happens if many examples have wrong labels?
options: The AI fixes them by itself
quiz.explain: AI learns from what it's shown, including the mistakes.

quiz.question: Why show the AI apples of many colours and shapes?
options: So it recognises all kinds of apples
quiz.explain: The more varied the examples, the more kinds of apples it can recognise.

summary: AI learns patterns from lots of labelled examples. Clear, correct and varied examples teach it well; wrong ones teach it mistakes.
